features.source: Claimed at once by Spain, Russia, Britain and the United States, and settled by none of them. The Nootka conventions of the 1790s left Spain conceding access rather than sovereignty, so the coast stayed open.

Occupied jointly by Britain and the United States under the convention of 1818, which said in as many words that neither party's claim was prejudiced. Neither state held it, so it is drawn as belonging to neither — the boundary at the 49th parallel is drawn from the Oregon Treaty of 1846 and not a day earlier.
